decision_clause: Ruled out: a hand-maintained product-code allowlist per ticket — because "each of the 60 remaining tickets would need a coordinated census amendment, and the list drifts from the tickets it mirrors". Scope: packages/schema/{package.json,src/metric-registry.ts,test/metric-registry.test.ts}, scripts/validate-planning.mjs, specs/metrics.v0.json, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs. Lifecycle: active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is 0 bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree. In that tree, scripts/validate-planning.mjs still admits product code by *deriving* the owned set at run time from each ticket's own Markdown — it reads every file matching docs/tickets/.../*.md, parses the `## Exact ownership` bullets (splitting `path — symbol; path — symbol` pairs on the semicolon first, then taking each pair's head) and the `- Test file: \`...\`` line, and accumulates those into `ticketOwnedPaths` (lines 835-857). `productCodeFiles` is then every source-extension file that is neither in the separate control-plane list nor in that derived set, and any survivor fails closed via `unallowlisted product code: ...` (lines 859-868). No static, per-ticket enumeration of product-code paths exists in the validator or in any of the seven scope files; the only literal path list, `controlPlaneAllowlist` (line 809), enumerates validator/test-infrastructure files, is not keyed by ticket, is not the product-code set, and is unmodified. packages/schema/src/metric-registry.ts is likewise unchanged and does not yet enforce the envelope the task describes: `registry_id` and `source_contract` appear only as members of REGISTRY_FIELDS (line 69) with no value comparison, and `consumers` is checked only for non-emptiness (`REGISTRY_CONSUMERS_MISSING`, lines 144-145) with no exact-set, duplicate, or non-string membership check.
rationale: The decision forbids one specific mechanism: a product-code allowlist maintained by hand, ticket by ticket, that would need a coordinated census amendment for each of the 60 remaining tickets. The finished tree does not introduce such a mechanism — it introduces nothing at all, since the diff is empty and every scope file matches the base. The admission mechanism that remains is the approved one, and it is structurally the opposite of what was ruled out: the census is recomputed from the ticket files themselves on every run, so adding a ticket that claims a path requires no edit to any list, which is precisely the drift the decision was written to prevent. I checked the one hand-maintained literal list in the validator (`controlPlaneAllowlist`) and it is a control-plane/test-infrastructure set, not a per-ticket product-code set, and it is untouched. Separately, and not bearing on this label: the task's actual requirements are unimplemented — metric-registry.ts performs no exact-value check on `registry_id` or `source_contract` and only rejects an empty `consumers` array, so a registry with a missing, added, duplicated, or non-string consumer, or with either provenance field changed, would still validate. That is a completeness failure of the task, not a breach of the recorded decision, and the two questions are answered separately. I chose COMPLIANT rather than INDETERMINATE because the empty diff resolves the decision question the same way under either reading of why it is empty: whether the change was never made or merely never captured, the tree in front of me contains no per-ticket hand-maintained product-code allowlist.
